newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Prominent Nigerian politician Sam Ikoku dies.
newsitem.headline: Prominent Nigerian politician Sam Ikoku dies.

text.p: The deputy chairman of the committee responsible for implementing Nigeria's transition to civilian rule, Sam Goomsu Ikoku, died on Thursday at the age of 71, local media reported on Friday.

They quoted his eldest son, Sam, as saying his father died in his home town of Awka in eastern Nigeria where he was on assignment to supervise the re-running of local council elections. The cause of death was not given.
Ikoku was a close adviser of military ruler General Sani Abacha.

One of Nigeria's most controversial politicians, he was general secretary of the opposition Action Group in the 1960s and was charged with treason, but before his trial began he fled to Ghana where he was close to the then President Kwame Nkrumah.

Ikoku abandoned opposition politics in the 1980s and campaigned for a system of government called "diarchy" under which the military and politicians would share power to end the cycle of coups in Nigeria.

As deputy chairman of the committee overseeing Abacha's programme for transition to civilian rule, he had said that the plan would fail if politicians did not show they were mature enough to govern Africa's most populous nation.
